authoredNote: Written AFTER the fix, and honestly labelled: the RULES below come from the Svelte 5 language (a destructuring pattern binds its value positions, reads its computed keys and its default values, and a property name is neither) and from the corpus files named in the fixture header — not from watching the analyzer. The line pins were read off the post-fix run and each was then checked against the fixture's own text: `count` is written on 65, `default_arg` on 69, `firstString` and `labelKey` on 73, `th` on 78 and 88, `defaultHeight` on 83, `pick` and `obj` on 102.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass, closing the last measured MISSING class on the `uses` label. A template BINDING PATTERN has read positions and binding positions; the flat word collector put every word in the SHADOW set, so it lost reads (`{#snippet counter(c = count)}` binds `c` and reads `count`) and fabricated shadows (`{#each xs as { a: b }}` binds `b` alone, so registering `a` silenced a member named `a` for the whole block). Measured before: the grammar-derived oracle named 35 unpublished template reads, 27 of them this class, over 81 corpus sites carrying a computed key or a default. The forbid rows below are the class's other half — the property names, the bindings, the type annotations and the literal defaults must NOT be published, because a reader that widens rather than splits converts 27 missing edges into fabricated ones.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE ORDERING RULE, and the one row a reader that collects all reads before all bindings fails. `{ idx, [idx - 1]: last }` binds the script member `idx` in the FIRST entry, so the computed key's `idx` reads a template-local and must publish nothing. `idx` is a declared script member precisely so this is observable in the payload: an unbound name would publish no edge either way and the row would assert nothing. No `line_number` is pinned, on purpose — a reader that un-shadows the name publishes the false read TWICE (once at the computed key, once at the `{idx}` in the body), and pinning one line would let the other through.
the value side of the computed-key entry binds
the VALUE side of `[firstString]: firstProp` binds; it is never a member read
same
`[`leng${th}`]: length2` — `length2` is the bound value, `th` is the read
same
the value side of the computed-key entry binds
a shorthand entry binds
`species = 'unknown'` binds `species`; the default is a string literal and reads nothing

`kilogram: weight = 50` — `kilogram` is a PROPERTY NAME and `weight` is the bound value. Neither is a read. `weight` is also read by `pound`'s default in the corpus shape, which is why the corpus file `each-block-destructured-default` is the one that measures the whole rule; here it is pinned as forbidden so a rename key cannot be mistaken for a read.
`kilogram` is a property name in a binding pattern, never a member read — the FALSE-SHADOW half of the defect, pinned so a future widening is caught
`...props` is a REST binding, not a read. (The body writes `{props.kind}`, whose receiver `props` is template-local and whose leaf `kind` is never read either.)
a member LEAF is not a read — `{props.kind}` reads nothing, since `props` is local
the await-then value side binds
same
`height: h` — the value side binds; `height` is a property name (see the `kg` row)
the declaration-tag head's value side binds
`{ value = "hello" }` — a literal default reads nothing
a TypeScript parameter ANNOTATION (`c: number = 4`) names a type. It is neither a binding nor a read — registering it as a shadow would be a false shadow of a member named `number`.
same, from `d?: string = 'x'`

a keyword in a default value is not a member read. The character collector has no keyword table, so the pattern reader filters the names its own span introduced — and this row is what stops that filter from being widened into a name list that could delete a TRUE edge.
same class as `true`
